The Wayof Mercury

Frater Stropheus

Heart of the Temple, Mercury its Hinge, and all its Offices, co-conspirators in the Work: I bring you my whole self: my Voice, and my Joy, Will, and Intent. Deed into word. By my Birthright, the Door is open.

A practice kept in a notebook, by hand, between those words and their closing.

The Way of Mercury is a journaling practice with a god in it. At its heart is something disarmingly simple: write, then reread what you wrote before and answer it. Your notebook stops being a pile of pages you never open and becomes a running conversation with your past self. Every session ends with one small thing to carry into the world, and the next session asks whether you did it. That question, answered honestly, is the whole engine.

From there it opens into something wonderfully rich. The magick starts with a promise to yourself, kept, however small. Every kept promise makes your word a little heavier, and a heavy word is what makes a declaration land. Integrity isn’t the price of the magick; it is the magick. Honesty works as engineering rather than virtue, because a Book you lie to only gives you bad data.

The Temple is openly syncretic, assembled in the spirit of chaos magic and gathered with real care for its sources. Hermes, Thoth, and Mercury stand alongside Enoch and Metatron, Iris, Hestia, Ma’at, and a whole lineage of scribes, messengers, and tricksters. None of them is petitioned. They are met as co-conspirators, in the old sense of the word: to breathe together. The Temple doesn’t act for you; it breathes with the one who is already moving. Its founding story is the infant Hermes trading his stolen cattle for the lyre he invented, the theft turned into music. Here the trickster is bound by truth, and the only trick worth playing is on your own rigid stories.

The Way is also gentle. It never asks you to write about anything you aren’t ready for. Three lines count as a session, and after a long absence you don’t apologize, you just open the Door and greet the Book. Nothing is forgotten, but pages can be answered, because mercy is restoration rather than erasure. It promises no rescue and no results without action, and it gathers the research behind its techniques so you can judge it by its fruit.

It’s built especially for quick, scattered, curious minds: people full of ideas who struggle to land them. Quicksilver takes the shape of its vessel, and the Book becomes that vessel. Over time it grows a spirit of its own, the way a house becomes a home.

Best of all, it’s freely given. Copy it, change it, and give it away. If it works for you, pass the luck on.

Four books. Via Mercurii is the book of the Way: its first volume is the Way in brief, and all you need, and the volumes after it gather what the Way means, everything it says, a notebook set up, and the year. Liber Mercurii is for going deeper. The Seed and the Almanac are for keeping near your hand. Nothing here is required reading, and the practice begins with a pen and one honest page.

Via Mercurii

The book of the Way of Mercury, in five volumes, with the Seed at the front. I, The Practice: the Way in brief and complete on its own, from who you need to know to the prayers, the blessings, the year, and why it works. II, The Sayings: every principle, with what it means and how to keep it. III, The Words: everything the Way says, whole in one place, for the Door. IV, A Model Book: a notebook shown set up. V, The Almanac: the year at a glance and the sky in order, for any year.

Start here. Volume I is all you need to begin; the rest is there when you want it.

A Mercurial Almanac for 2027

The whole year on one page, to pin up, and every day of the Calendar set against one particular sky: the fixed feasts, Mercury’s own cycle from the ephemeris, turn by turn, and the Moon, with the days the two agree.

One year, dated; Volume V of Via Mercurii is the same almanac for any year. Keep it near the Book and mark the days you will actually keep.
